claim: Circulation of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) contributes to body axis formation and brain development.
source: Circulation of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) contributes to body axis formation and brain development.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general claim about CSF function, supported by the broader context of the study.

claim: The CSF flow in the central canal of 30 hpf zebrafish embryos is bidirectional.
source: Here, we investigated the unexplained origins of the CSF flow bidirectionality in the central canal of the spinal cord of 30 hpf zebrafish embryos and its impact on development.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that the study investigated CSF flow bidirectionality in the central canal.

claim: The CSF flow is generated locally by caudally-polarized motile cilia along the ventral wall of the central canal.
source: Experiments combined with modeling and simulations demonstrate that the CSF flow is generated locally by caudally-polarized motile cilia along the ventral wall of the central canal.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding based on experiments, modeling, and simulations.

claim: The closed geometry of the canal imposes the average flow rate to be null, explaining the reported bidirectionality.
source: The closed geometry of the canal imposes the average flow rate to be null, explaining the reported bidirectionality.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this as an explanation for bidirectionality based on geometric constraints.

claim: At 30 hpf, motile cilia ensure the proper formation of the central canal.
source: We also demonstrate that at this early stage, motile cilia ensure the proper formation of the central canal.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding about the role of motile cilia.

claim: The bidirectional flow accelerates the transport of particles in the CSF via a coupled convective-diffusive transport process.
source: Furthermore, we demonstrate that the bidirectional flow accelerates the transport of particles in the CSF via a coupled convective-diffusive transport process.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding about particle transport.

claim: Cilia activity combined with muscle contractions sustain the long-range transport of extracellular lipidic particles, enabling embryonic growth.
source: Our study demonstrates that cilia activity combined with muscle contractions sustain the long-range transport of extracellular lipidic particles, enabling embryonic growth.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this conclusion about the combined role of cilia and muscle contractions.

claim: Blood flow is the main carrier of glucose and oxygen in most organisms and is mostly driven by the pressure gradient caused by the heart pump.
source: Blood flow is the main carrier of glucose and oxygen in most organisms and is mostly driven by the pressure gradient caused by the heart pump (Fung, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Fung, 2013.

claim: Intestine, esophageal, and lymph flows rely on peristalsis, where muscle contractions drive the fluid in the direction of propagation of the contraction wave.
source: Intestine, esophageal, and lymph flows rely on peristalsis, where muscles contractions drive the fluid in the direction of propagation of the contraction wave (Fung and Yih, 1968; Goyal and Paterson, 2011; Hennig et al., 1999; Kim et al., 2017; Shapiro et al., 1969).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Cilia-driven flows are critical for left/right asymmetry in the developing embryos of many species including humans.
source: Cilia-driven flows are critical for left/right asymmetry in the developing embryos of many species including humans (Baker and Beales, 2009), in the Kupffer's vesicle in zebrafish (Ferreira et al., 2017; Supatto et al., 2008), and in the embryonic node in mammals (Essner, 2005; Nonaka et al., 2005; Okada et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The motility of cilia in brain ventricles is correlated with the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow in zebrafish.
source: The motility of cilia in brain ventricles is also correlated with the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow in zebrafish (Grimes et al., 2016; Kramer-Zucker et al., 2005; Olstad et al., 2018), African clawed frog (Hagenlocher et al., 2013; Miskevich, 2010) and rodents (Faubel et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: CSF circulation was recently shown to be critical for body axis formation in the embryo and spine morphogenesis in zebrafish juveniles and adults.
source: CSF circulation was recently shown to be critical for body axis formation in the embryo and spine morphogenesis in zebrafish juveniles and adults (Grimes et al., 2016; Van Gennip et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: During embryogenesis, mutations that affect cilia polarity or motility and ciliogenesis lead to defects in transport along the rostrocaudal axis and body axis formation.
source: During embryogenesis, mutations that affect cilia polarity or motility and ciliogenesis lead to defects in transport along the rostrocaudal axis and body axis formation (Boswell and Ciruna, 2017; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: In 24–30 hr post fertilization (hpf) zebrafish embryos, the CSF flows bidirectionally.
source: We recently showed in 24–30 hr post fertilization (hpf) zebrafish embryos that the CSF flows bidirectionally (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018; Sternberg et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to the authors' previous work.

claim: Body-axis defects observed in mutants with defective cilia appear by 30 hpf, before cilia of the brain ventricles become motile.
source: Interestingly, body-axis defects observed in mutants with defective cilia appear by 30 hpf, that is, a few hours before cilia of the brain ventricles become motile and a directed CSF flow emerges in the ventricles (Fame et al., 2016; Olstad et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and temporal observations.

claim: Proper dynamics of CSF flow in the central canal, rather than in the brain ventricles, is critical for embryonic development.
source: This result suggests that proper dynamics of CSF flow in the central canal, rather than in the brain ventricles, is critical for embryonic development.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the timing of defects relative to cilia motility in different regions.

claim: Motile cilia are required to form the lumen of the central canal.
source: We first show that motile cilia are required to form the lumen of the central canal, as the canal has a reduced diameter in mutants with defective cilia.
evidence: This statement is based on observations in mutants with defective cilia.

claim: The canal has a reduced diameter in mutants with defective cilia.
source: We first show that motile cilia are required to form the lumen of the central canal, as the canal has a reduced diameter in mutants with defective cilia.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study.

claim: The bidirectional CSF flow in the central canal is enhanced by muscle contractions.
source: We demonstrate that this bidirectional CSF flow in the central canal is enhanced by muscle contractions, which accelerate bidirectional transport of particles both rostrally and caudally.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: Muscle contractions accelerate bidirectional transport of particles both rostrally and caudally.
source: We demonstrate that this bidirectional CSF flow in the central canal is enhanced by muscle contractions, which accelerate bidirectional transport of particles both rostrally and caudally.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: The CSF flows unidirectionally from the diencephalic/mesencephalic ventricle to the entrance of the central canal.
source: We show that the CSF flows unidirectionally from the diencephalic/mesencephalic ventricle to the entrance of the central canal, and that in vivo two-photon ablation of this connection leads to a reduction in size of embryos.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: In vivo two-photon ablation of the connection between the diencephalic/mesencephalic ventricle and the central canal leads to a reduction in size of embryos.
source: We show that the CSF flows unidirectionally from the diencephalic/mesencephalic ventricle to the entrance of the central canal, and that in vivo two-photon ablation of this connection leads to a reduction in size of embryos.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: Long-range CSF transport plays a role in growth during embryogenesis.
source: It suggests a role for long-range CSF transport in growth during embryogenesis.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the ablation experiments.

claim: The typical velocity profile in the central canal is bimodal with positive flow (rostral to caudal) in the ventral side and negative flow (caudal to rostral) in the dorsal side.
source: The typical velocity profile is bimodal with positive flow (rostral to caudal) in the ventral side and negative flow (caudal to rostral) in the dorsal side, and reverses close to the center of the CC (relative D-V position = 0.53, Figure 1D from 110 wild type (WT) embryos each imaged in two rostro-caudal positions).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from measurements in 110 WT embryos, with reference to Figure 1D.

claim: The velocity profile reverses close to the center of the central canal at relative D-V position = 0.53.
source: The typical velocity profile is bimodal with positive flow (rostral to caudal) in the ventral side and negative flow (caudal to rostral) in the dorsal side, and reverses close to the center of the CC (relative D-V position = 0.53, Figure 1D from 110 wild type (WT) embryos each imaged in two rostro-caudal positions).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from measurements in 110 WT embryos, with reference to Figure 1D.

claim: Velocity profiles exhibit a maximal speed of 4.78 ± 0.79 μm.s−1 ventrally at relative D-V position = 0.29 on average.
source: Velocity profiles exhibit a maximal speed of 4.78 ± 0.79 μm.s−1 (relative D-V position = 0.29 on average) ventrally and a minimal speed of - 4.80 ± 0.82 μm.s−1 (relative D-V position = 0.82 on average) dorsally (Figure 1B1 and B2).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from velocity profile measurements, with reference to Figure 1B1 and B2.

claim: Velocity profiles exhibit a minimal speed of - 4.80 ± 0.82 μm.s−1 dorsally at relative D-V position = 0.82 on average.
source: Velocity profiles exhibit a maximal speed of 4.78 ± 0.79 μm.s−1 (relative D-V position = 0.29 on average) ventrally and a minimal speed of - 4.80 ± 0.82 μm.s−1 (relative D-V position = 0.82 on average) dorsally (Figure 1B1 and B2).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from velocity profile measurements, with reference to Figure 1B1 and B2.

claim: The profiles are nearly symmetrical with relative D-V position at the zero-crossing = 0.53 on average.
source: The profiles are nearly symmetrical (relative D-V position at the zero-crossing = 0.53 on average).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from velocity profile measurements.

claim: The average speed throughout the central canal is null (- 0.02 ± 0.15 μm.s−1).
source: Similarly, the average speed throughout the CC is null (- 0.02 ± 0.15 μm.s−1).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from velocity profile measurements.

claim: The average CSF flow rate through a section of the central canal is null.
source: This implies that the average CSF flow rate through a section of CC is null as well.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the null average speed.

claim: A global pressure gradient as the unique driver of the flow in the central canal is refuted.
source: According to Poiseuille's relationship, this refutes the hypothesis of a global pressure gradient as the unique driver of the flow in the CC.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on Poiseuille's relationship and the null average flow rate.

claim: The central canal geometry mostly corresponds to a cylinder of diameter 8.9 ± 0.9 μm.
source: The CC geometry, as estimated by TexasRed-Dextran (3,000 MW) injections, mostly corresponds to a cylinder (Figure 2A1 and A2) of diameter 8.9 ± 0.9 μm (129 WT embryos, Figure 2A3).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from measurements in 129 WT embryos, with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: Density and motility of cilia are higher in the ventral central canal.
source: Density and motility of cilia are higher in the ventral CC as previously reported (Borovina et al., 2010; Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018; Sternberg et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a finding consistent with previous reports, supported by citations.

claim: Some cilia beat at high frequency (up to 45 Hz) with a single frequency pattern.
source: While some cilia beat at high frequency (up to45 Hz, see Materials and methods) with a single frequency pattern, others beat at lower frequency (~13 Hz) with more complex and irregular patterns.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from cilia dynamics analysis.

claim: Some cilia beat at lower frequency (~13 Hz) with more complex and irregular patterns.
source: While some cilia beat at high frequency (up to45 Hz, see Materials and methods) with a single frequency pattern, others beat at lower frequency (~13 Hz) with more complex and irregular patterns.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from cilia dynamics analysis.

claim: Motile ventral cilia were four times more numerous than the dorsal ones.
source: Motile ventral cilia were four times more numerous than the dorsal ones.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from quantification of cilia.

claim: Ventral motile cilia were typically 5.8 μm long and beat at 38.1 Hz with a caudal tilt of 62.6° towards the tail.
source: Ventral motile cilia were typically 5.8 μm long and beat at 38.1 Hz with a caudal tilt of 62.6° towards the tail (median of the absolute value, see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from quantification of cilia parameters.

claim: Ventral cilia length corresponds to a height of 2.7 μm in the central canal, representing a bit less than half of the central canal on the ventral side.
source: This cilia length corresponds to a height of 2.7 μm in the CC, representing a bit less than half of the CC on the ventral side.
evidence: This is stated as a calculation based on cilia length measurements.

claim: The beating frequencies measured were higher than the 12–15 Hz previously reported in zebrafish central canal.
source: The beating frequencies we measured were higher than the 12–15 Hz previously reported in zebrafish CC (Kramer-Zucker et al., 2005) (see Materials and methods for a possible explanation), but are consistent with beating frequencies of ependymal cilia located in the brain ventricles of rats (Smith et al., 2012) and zebrafish larvae (Olstad et al., 2018; Smith et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with previous reports, supported by citations.

claim: The measured beating frequencies are consistent with beating frequencies of ependymal cilia located in the brain ventricles of rats and zebrafish larvae.
source: The beating frequencies we measured were higher than the 12–15 Hz previously reported in zebrafish CC (Kramer-Zucker et al., 2005) (see Materials and methods for a possible explanation), but are consistent with beating frequencies of ependymal cilia located in the brain ventricles of rats (Smith et al., 2012) and zebrafish larvae (Olstad et al., 2018; Smith et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with other reports, supported by citations.

claim: Dorsal motile cilia were sparse and evenly distributed along the rostro-caudal axis.
source: Dorsal motile cilia were sparse and evenly distributed along the rostro-caudal axis: they beat with a slightly smaller central frequency (~32 Hz, Figure 2C2), but exhibited similar properties to ventral cilia otherwise (see Figure 2C3, 4, caudal polarization of 59.7 °, length of 5.5 μm).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from quantification of dorsal cilia, with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: Dorsal motile cilia beat with a slightly smaller central frequency (~32 Hz).
source: Dorsal motile cilia were sparse and evenly distributed along the rostro-caudal axis: they beat with a slightly smaller central frequency (~32 Hz, Figure 2C2), but exhibited similar properties to ventral cilia otherwise (see Figure 2C3, 4, caudal polarization of 59.7 °, length of 5.5 μm).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from quantification of dorsal cilia, with reference to Figure 2C2.

claim: Dorsal motile cilia have a caudal polarization of 59.7° and length of 5.5 μm.
source: Dorsal motile cilia were sparse and evenly distributed along the rostro-caudal axis: they beat with a slightly smaller central frequency (~32 Hz, Figure 2C2), but exhibited similar properties to ventral cilia otherwise (see Figure 2C3, 4, caudal polarization of 59.7 °, length of 5.5 μm).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from quantification of dorsal cilia, with reference to Figure 2C3, 4.

claim: Theoretical and numerical predictions are in good agreement with the 57 velocity profiles measured in vivo.
source: Theoretical and numerical predictions are in good agreement with the 57 velocity profiles measured in vivo and tested here (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between model predictions and experimental data, with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Numerical simulations show that recirculation regions appear between spots of constant volume force.
source: With this 'sparse cilia' model, numerical simulations show that recirculation regions appear between these spots (Figure 3C2).
evidence: This is stated as a result from numerical simulations, with reference to Figure 3C2.

claim: Differences in beating frequency between active neighboring cilia lead to the emergence of recirculation regions.
source: We can further show that differences in beating frequency between active neighboring cilia lead to the emergence of the same recirculation regions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the model, with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: In all mutants with defective cilia (elipsa, lrrc50, foxj1anw2, kurly), no particles entered the central canal even several hours post injection in anaesthetized mutant embryos.
source: In all these mutants with defective cilia, we injected beads in the DV/MV, but we could not observe the beads transported inside the CC. In anaesthetized mutant embryos, no particles entered the CC even several hours post injection, as illustrated here in elipsa embryos (Figure 4A1 and A2).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments in mutants, with reference to Figure 4A1 and A2.

claim: Long-range transport of beads down the central canal is altered in mutants with defective cilia.
source: This observation is consistent with previous reports (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2018) showing that long-range transport of beads down the central canal is altered in mutants with defective cilia.
evidence: This is stated as a finding consistent with previous reports, supported by citations.

claim: The central canal diameter was dramatically reduced in all mutants tested: elipsa, lrrc50, foxj1anw2, and kurly.
source: Surprisingly, we observed that the CC diameter was dramatically reduced in all mutants tested: elipsa, lrrc50, foxj1anw2, and kurly (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments in mutants, with reference to Figure 4B,C.

claim: The central canal is flattened along the D-V axis and not as straight as control siblings in mutants with defective cilia.
source: Although the CC forms in these mutants, it is flattened along the D-V axis and not as straight as control siblings (Figure 4B1, B2 and C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments in mutants, with reference to Figure 4B1, B2 and C.

claim: For scospondinicm15/icm15 mutants, which are curled down but exhibit normal cilia activity, no difference in the central canal diameter was measured.
source: In order to evaluate whether these features could be due to the convex body curvature of the embryos, we analyzed the CC structure of mutant embryos scospondinicm15/icm15, which are also curled down but exhibit normal cilia activity (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018). For these mutants, we did not measure any difference in the CC diameter.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments in scospondin mutants, supported by a citation.

claim: Cilia integrity and motility are critical to properly form the central canal and instruct its diameter and straightness.
source: This observation suggests that cilia integrity and motility are critical to properly form the CC and instruct its diameter and straightness.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the observations in mutants.

claim: Allowing mutant embryos to spontaneously twitch facilitated the transport of beads down the central canal.
source: However, we noticed that allowing mutant embryos to spontaneously twitch (by not anesthetizing them before imaging) facilitated the transport of beads down the CC (see next section for the characterization of the effect of muscle contraction on CSF flow).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments in mutants.

claim: Fluorescent beads in the central canal of elipsa and kurly mostly undergo random Brownian motion, but some allow to measure a residual flow with many recirculation zones.
source: By using the effect of muscle contractions, we were able to get beads down the CC in mutants with a moderate reduction of the CC diameter, such as elipsa and kurly. Fluorescent beads in the CC of elipsa and kurly mostly undergo random Brownian motion, but some allow to measure a residual flow with many recirculation zones (Video 4), in good agreement with the predictions of the sparse cilia model.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments in mutants, with reference to Video 4.

claim: The bidirectional CSF flow in the central canal is generated locally and does not rely on a global pressure gradient generated in the ventricles.
source: It is also predicted that the bidirectional CSF flow in the CC is generated locally and does not rely on a global pressure gradient generated in the ventricles.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction from the model.

claim: Even after large regions without cilia and local flow, the CSF flow in more caudal regions can show a bidirectional flow, as long as motile cilia beat locally in the ventral region.
source: This is confirmed by multiple observations: i) even after large regions without cilia and local flow, the CSF flow in more caudal regions can show a bidirectional flow, as long as motile cilia beat locally in the ventral region (as predicted by Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated as an observation confirming the model prediction, with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: When a portion of the central canal of around 200 μm in length is isolated by using photoablation to block flow on both extremities, the canal kept its diameter at the center and the CSF still flowed bidirectionally.
source: ii) When a portion of the CC of around 200 μm in length is isolated by using photoablation to block flow on both extremities (see Materials and methods and Figure 4D1), the canal kept its diameter at the center and the CSF still flowed bidirectionally (Video 5) with a similar velocity profile (Figure 4D2).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from photoablation experiments, with reference to Figure 4D1, D2 and Video 5.

claim: Following each muscle contraction, rapid displacements of CSF were observed in either the caudal or rostral direction, followed by a slower counter-flow in the opposite direction.
source: Following each contraction, rapid displacements of CSF (too fast to be properly characterized) were observed in either the caudal or rostral direction, followed by a slower counter-flow in the opposite direction, whose velocity decayed until the original bidirectional flow is recovered (Figure 5B and C, Video 6, Video 7).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments in contracting embryos, with reference to Figure 5B and C, Video 6, Video 7.

claim: The average CSF flow throughout the entire central canal section is correlated with the instantaneous muscle contractions.
source: The average CSF flow throughout the entire CC section is correlated with the instantaneous muscle contractions (Figure 5D) and showed a sudden increase after contractions.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments in contracting embryos, with reference to Figure 5D.

claim: A robust flow rate increase was observed after each contraction.
source: By comparing the increase in CSF flow over 5 s after each contraction with the contraction strength, we observed a robust flow rate increase after each contraction (Figure 5E; 204 contractions from 22 WT embryos).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments in contracting embryos, with reference to Figure 5E.

claim: No correlation was found between the flow direction and estimates of the contraction direction or strength.
source: However, we did not find any correlation between the flow direction and estimates of the contraction direction or strength.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments in contracting embryos.

claim: Body contractions enhance transport of beads in mutants with defective cilia.
source: Body contractions also enhance transport of beads in mutants with defective cilia, as mentioned in the previous section (Video 4).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments in mutants, with reference to Video 4.

claim: No significant difference in the central canal diameter was detected during the muscle contractions.
source: As no significant difference in the CC diameter was detected during the muscle contractions, we propose that the reported enhancement of CSF flow is not due to a local variation of the CC diameter, but instead due to a change in the volume of the brain ventricles that occurs during muscle contraction at larval stage (Olstad et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments in contracting embryos, with a citation.

claim: The enhancement of CSF flow is due to a change in the volume of the brain ventricles that occurs during muscle contraction at larval stage.
source: As no significant difference in the CC diameter was detected during the muscle contractions, we propose that the reported enhancement of CSF flow is not due to a local variation of the CC diameter, but instead due to a change in the volume of the brain ventricles that occurs during muscle contraction at larval stage (Olstad et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a proposed explanation, with a citation.

claim: CSF long-range transport of nanoparticles has characteristics of both passive diffusion and active transport.
source: Here, we first demonstrate experimentally that CSF long-range transport of nanoparticles has characteristics of both passive diffusion and active transport.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: The particle transport follows an apparent diffusive law, as the propagation front of nanoparticles progresses with the square root of time.
source: The particle transport follows an apparent diffusive law, as the propagation front of nanoparticles progresses with the square root of time (Zhang et al., 2018) and this propagation is found to be slower for larger particle size (Figure 6A1 and A2).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study, with a citation and reference to Figure 6A1 and A2.

claim: The propagation of nanoparticles is found to be slower for larger particle size.
source: The particle transport follows an apparent diffusive law, as the propagation front of nanoparticles progresses with the square root of time (Zhang et al., 2018) and this propagation is found to be slower for larger particle size (Figure 6A1 and A2).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study, with reference to Figure 6A1 and A2.

claim: The propagation front of 20 nm-diameter fluorescent beads is accelerated by muscle contractions, when the local CSF flow velocity is increased.
source: On the other hand, the propagation front of 20 nm-diameter fluorescent beads is accelerated by muscle contractions, when the local CSF flow velocity is increased (Figure 6A2 and A3).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study, with reference to Figure 6A2 and A3.

claim: 20 nm-diameter fluorescent beads injected in the DV/MV are found to travel through the entire length of central canal (~2 mm) in about two hours.
source: Indeed, 20 nm-diameter fluorescent beads injected in the DV/MV are found to travel through the entire length of CC (~2 mm) in about two hours (Figure 6A2), far from the timescales expected for passive diffusion (over one day) or pure ballistic transport at the speed of the flow (with V = 5 μm/s, this would lead to less than 10 min).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study, with reference to Figure 6A2.

claim: The effective diffusivity is higher in the case of contracting embryos compared to paralyzed embryos.
source: In vivo front tracking experiments illustrate this flow-induced accelerated transport of 20 nm nanoparticles in paralyzed and contracting zebrafish embryos (Figure 6D). While both contracting and paralyzed embryos exhibit a diffusive-like transport, the effective diffusivity is higher in the case of contracting embryos.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study, with reference to Figure 6D.

claim: Muscle contractions can increase the long-range transport efficiency.
source: It confirms that muscle contractions can increase the long-range transport efficiency (an increase of the steady bidirectional velocity would have similar effects, Figure 6C1).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study, with reference to Figure 6C1.

claim: The transport is predicted to be enhanced in both rostro-caudal and caudo-rostral directions.
source: Interestingly, the transport is predicted to be enhanced in both rostro-caudal and caudo-rostral directions, which is confirmed by in vivo experiments.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction from the model confirmed by experiments.

claim: When injected locally in the caudal part of the central canal, fluorescent nanobeads are transported rostrally towards the brain ventricles.
source: When injected locally in the caudal part of the CC, fluorescent nanobeads are indeed transported rostrally towards the brain ventricles (Figure 6E1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study, with reference to Figure 6E1.

claim: The reverse transport is sped up in contracting embryos.
source: Similarly to rostral-to-caudal transport, the reverse transport is sped up incontracting embryos (Figure 6E2).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study, with reference to Figure 6E2.

claim: At 30 hpf, cilia in the brain ventricles are mostly non-motile.
source: At this stage, cilia in the brain ventricles are mostly non-motile (Olstad et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a fact, with a citation.

claim: At 30 hpf, CSF flow in the brain ventricles is mostly Brownian, although the heart beat is responsible for a pulsatile component to the flow at the heart beat frequency.
source: At this stage, CSF flow in the brain ventricles is mostly Brownian, although the heart beat is responsible for a pulsatile component to the flow at the heart beat frequency (Video 8), as previously observed (Fame et al., 2016; Olstad et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study, with citations and reference to Video 8.

claim: Before 30 hpf CSF flow in the brain ventricles does not contribute to the overall CSF circulation.
source: Our observations indicate that before 30 hpf CSF flow in the brain ventricles does not contribute to the overall CSF circulation.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the observations.

claim: The diameter of the ventral opening of the RV primitive lumen is smaller than the central canal diameter (7.1 ± 0.7 μm) and is 233 ± 24 μm long.
source: We measured that the diameter of this ventral opening is smaller than the CC diameter (7.1 ± 0.7 μm) and is 233 ± 24 μm long (Figure 7A and B – green arrow, 7C,11 embryos, Video 9) and that few motile cilia enable there a unidirectional flow from rostral to caudal, that is towards the CC (Video 10).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from measurements in 11 embryos, with reference to Figure 7A, B, C and Video 9, 10.

claim: Few motile cilia enable a unidirectional flow from rostral to caudal in the ventral opening of the RV primitive lumen.
source: We measured that the diameter of this ventral opening is smaller than the CC diameter (7.1 ± 0.7 μm) and is 233 ± 24 μm long (Figure 7A and B – green arrow, 7C,11 embryos, Video 9) and that few motile cilia enable there a unidirectional flow from rostral to caudal, that is towards the CC (Video 10).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study, with reference to Video 10.

claim: This fast and unidirectional flow follows a parabolic Poiseuille-like velocity profile with a maximum speed of 15 μm / s.
source: This fast and unidirectional flow follows a parabolic Poiseuille-like velocity profile with a maximum speed of 15 μm / s (Figure 7D1 and D2).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study, with reference to Figure 7D1 and D2.

claim: The central canal primitive lumen is composed of two main openings, with a very narrow but continuous connection between the two.
source: The CC pL is indeed composed of two main openings, with a very narrow but continuous connection between the two (Kondrychyn et al., 2013, Ribeiro et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as a fact, with citations.

claim: The apical domains of the two openings of the central canal primitive lumen, marked with the tight junctions protein ZO-1, are closely-spaced, so that CSF flow is independent in each opening.
source: We observed that the apical domains of the two openings of the CC pL, marked with the tight junctions protein ZO-1, are closely-spaced, so that CSF flow is independent in each opening (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study, with reference to Figure 7E.

claim: The central canal ventral and dorsal openings converge into a single opening, dense in motile cilia, in the caudal part of the spinal cord.
source: Interestingly, we found that the CC ventral and dorsal openings converge into a single opening, dense in motile cilia, in the caudal part of the spinal cord (Figure 7 E2, Video 12).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study, with reference to Figure 7 E2 and Video 12.

claim: During development, dorsal and ventral openings of the central canal primitive lumen converge ventrally at three dpf.
source: During development, as it has already been partly described in rodents and zebrafish (Sevc et al., 2009; Kondrychyn et al., 2013, Ribeiro et al., 2017), dorsal and ventral openings of the CC pL converge ventrally at three dpf (Figure 7F) to finally merge into a single central canal lumen at five dpf (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study, with citations and reference to Figure 7F.

claim: Dorsal and ventral openings of the central canal primitive lumen finally merge into a single central canal lumen at five dpf.
source: During development, as it has already been partly described in rodents and zebrafish (Sevc et al., 2009; Kondrychyn et al., 2013, Ribeiro et al., 2017), dorsal and ventral openings of the CC pL converge ventrally at three dpf (Figure 7F) to finally merge into a single central canal lumen at five dpf (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study, with citations and reference to Figure 7G.

claim: Half of the ablated larvae were shorter in length than siblings that underwent a control ablation of the yolk extension or had no ablation, 30 hr after ablation at the beginning of the central canal.
source: We performed 2-photon mediated photo-ablations at the beginning of the CC to disconnect the CC from the brain ventricles (Figure 8A1 and A2). We found that 30 hr after ablation, half of the ablated larvae were shorter in length than siblings that underwent a control ablation of the yolk extension or had no ablation (Figure 8B1 and B2).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from ablation experiments, with reference to Figure 8A1, A2, B1 and B2.

claim: Larvae with the opening ablated had an increase in body-axis curvature.
source: Larvae with the opening ablated had an increase in body-axis curvature (Figure 8C1 and C2).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from ablation experiments, with reference to Figure 8C1 and C2.

claim: Global CSF circulation contributes to embryonic growth.
source: These experiments indicate that global CSF circulation contributes to embryonic growth, and suggest that the transport of particles between brain and spinal cord is a critical process for development.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the ablation experiments.

claim: The transport of particles between brain and spinal cord is a critical process for development.
source: These experiments indicate that global CSF circulation contributes to embryonic growth, and suggest that the transport of particles between brain and spinal cord is a critical process for development.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the ablation experiments.

claim: Full field optical coherence tomography imaging of 30 hpf embryos reveals high density of secreted vesicles in central canal.
source: In order to find particles that could be efficiently transported by the bidirectional flow, we investigated the content of the CSF and identified abundant extracellular vesicles using the label-free imaging technique, full field optical coherence tomography (Figure 8D and Video 13).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study, with reference to Figure 8D and Video 13.

claim: Numerous vesicles with high lipids or proteins content filled the central canal.
source: Numerous vesicles with high lipids or proteins content filled the CC, in agreement with previous observations (Sternberg et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study, with a citation.

claim: Some of the particles in the CSF may correspond to exosomes.
source: Fluorescent labeling of CD63 (Video 14, Materials and methods) and electron microscopy with immunogold labeling of exosomes suggested that some of these particles may correspond to exosomes in the CSF (Figure 8E, Materials and methods) (Verweij et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study, with a citation and reference to Figure 8E and Video 14.

claim: Electron microscopy reveals a variety of other extracellular vesicles, such as lipoparticles, microvesicles.
source: Electron microscopy also reveals a variety of other extracellular vesicles, such as lipoparticles, microvesicles.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from electron microscopy.

claim: The diameter of these vesicles ranges between 50 and 250 nm.
source: The diameter of these vesicles ranges between 50 and 250 nm (Figure 8E), typically in a regime where Taylor-Aris dispersion is important.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from electron microscopy, with reference to Figure 8E.

claim: The bidirectional flow of endogenous extracellular vesicles can be put in evidence in the central canal using full field optical coherence tomography as well as fluorescence live imaging.
source: The bidirectional flow of endogenous extracellular vesicles can be put in evidence in the CC using full field optical coherence tomography as well as fluorescence live imaging (Video 13, Video 14).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study, with reference to Video 13 and Video 14.

claim: The effective CSF circulation contributes to embryonic growth via the transport of extracellular vesicles between brain and spinal cord.
source: Altogether, our works suggests that the effective CSF circulation contributes to embryonic growth via the transport of extracellular vesicles between brain and spinal cord.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study.

claim: A steady bidirectional CSF flow is driven by ventral motile cilia.
source: In this study, we performed quantification of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulation in zebrafish embryos. By combining experiments and modeling, we demonstrated that a steady bidirectional CSF flow is driven by ventral motile cilia and that body movements create additional transient flows.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Body movements create additional transient flows.
source: In this study, we performed quantification of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulation in zebrafish embryos. By combining experiments and modeling, we demonstrated that a steady bidirectional CSF flow is driven by ventral motile cilia and that body movements create additional transient flows.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study.

claim: These two driving forces (cilia and body movements) accelerate the long-range transport of all particles larger than 10 nm, including the many macromolecules and extracellular vesicles present in the central canal.
source: These two driving forces accelerate the long-range transport of all particles larger than 10 nm, including the many macromolecules and extracellular vesicles present in the CC.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Fast transport both from brain to spinal cord, and from spinal cord to the brain, is critical for normal embryonic development.
source: This permits fast transport both from brain to spinal cord, and from spinal cord to the brain, which is critical for normal embryonic development.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study.

claim: The study focused on embryogenesis as this is a critical period when CSF is most concentrated in secreted extracellular lipid vesicles.
source: Our study focused on embryogenesis as this is a critical period when CSF is most concentrated in secreted extracellular lipid vesicles (Bachy et al., 2008; Tietje et al., 2014), and when blood flow along the body is not established to transport key molecules.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for the study focus, with citations.

claim: During embryogenesis, blood flow along the body is not established to transport key molecules.
source: Our study focused on embryogenesis as this is a critical period when CSF is most concentrated in secreted extracellular lipid vesicles (Bachy et al., 2008; Tietje et al., 2014), and when blood flow along the body is not established to transport key molecules.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for the study focus.

claim: The work predicts the establishment of a positive pressure in the central canal, increasing linearly towards the caudal direction.
source: Our work predicts the establishment of a positive pressure in the CC, increasing linearly towards the caudal direction (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a prediction from the model, with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: This inner pressure is decreased as the density of motile cilia is lower.
source: This inner pressure is decreased as the density of motile cilia is lower.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction from the model.

claim: Among other roles related to transport of chemical cues or mechano-sensing, the cilia motility ensures the integrity of the central canal, which is necessary for proper body axis formation.
source: This suggests that, among other roles related to transport of chemical cues or mechano-sensing, the cilia motility ensures the integrity of the CC, which is necessary for proper body axis formation.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the findings.

claim: Small veins have been reported to collapse under a decrease of inner pressure.
source: Interestingly, small veins have also been reported to collapse under a decrease of inner pressure (Fung, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison, with a citation.

claim: During some fixation processes, if the structure is not maintained fast enough, the loss of cilia activity should lead to a decrease of the inner pressure and to the collapse of the central canal.
source: During some fixation processes, if the structure is not maintained fast enough, the loss of cilia activity should lead to a decrease of the inner pressure and to the collapse of the CC.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation about fixation processes.

claim: Mutants with defective cilia were unable to maintain an open central canal.
source: We report that mutants with defective cilia were unable to maintain an open CC.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: Elipsa and kurly embryos with partial loss of cilia motility show intermediate phenotypes, with some regions open and other constrained, and with open regions showing bidirectional flow with a higher density of recirculation zones.
source: Elipsa and kurly embryos with partial loss of cilia motility show intermediate phenotypes, with some regions open and other constrained, and with open regions showing bidirectional flow with a higher density of recirculation zones.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: These flow patterns are predicted by the sparse cilia model.
source: These flow patterns are predicted by the sparse cilia model (Figure 3C), since a few cilia remain motile in kurly embryos (Jaffe et al., 2016) and in elipsa between 24 hpf and 30 hpf (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between model predictions and observations, with citations and reference to Figure 3C.

claim: The sparse cilia model accounts for the reduced long-range transport previously observed in kif3b mutants, where cilia density is reduced.
source: It also accounts for the reduced long-range transport previously observed in kif3b mutants, where cilia density is reduced (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for previous observations, with a citation.

claim: Foxj1a mutant embryos showing ependymal cells with defective cilia have an almost closed central canal.
source: In contrast, foxj1a mutant embryos showing ependymal cells with defective cilia (Yu et al., 2008) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) have an almost closed CC.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the study, with a citation and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The motile cilia generating the flow and maintaining the central canal geometry originate from ependymal cells only.
source: This observation strongly suggests that the motile cilia generating the flow and maintaining the CC geometry originate from ependymal cells only, while the remaining cilia that probably belong to CSF-contacting neurons (Böhm et al., 2016) are too short and not dense enough to generate a stable CC (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the observations, with a citation and reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: A specific circulation between the ventricles and the central canal is established at embryonic stage.
source: In this study, we finally described the global circulation of CSF through transient openings of the pL of the brain ventricles and the CC, and showed that a specific circulation between the ventricles and the CC is established at embryonic stage.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: This circulation between the ventricles and the central canal was required for normal development.
source: We showed that this circulation was required for normal development.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: This transient architecture and circulation within the primitive lumens in the developing brain and spinal cord may be specific to teleost species.
source: This transient architecture and circulation within the primitive lumens in the developing brain and spinal cord may be specific to teleost species, where the neural tube and ventricles form by tissue internalization and cavitation (Guo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a speculation, with a citation.

claim: In Amniotes such as mammals, the neural tube forms mainly by tissue folding and fusion.
source: In contrast, in Amniotes such as mammals, the neural tube forms mainly by tissue folding and fusion (Araya et al., 2016; Cearns et al., 2016; Lowery and Sive, 2004).
evidence: This is stated as a fact, with citations.

claim: There are evidences for similar appositions of ventricular walls in Amniotes.
source: However, there are evidences for similar appositions of ventricular walls in Amniotes (in mouse: Chen et al., 2017 and; in chicken: Halasi et al., 2012), and these developing structures would be interesting to study in other species.
evidence: This is stated as a fact, with citations.

claim: The force fv fits experimental data for an amplitude of 4000 N/m3, corresponding to a force of 10 pN generated by a single cilium occupying a volume of characteristic size 10 μm.
source: The latter fits experimental data for an amplitude of 4000 N/m3, corresponding to a force of 10 pN generated by a single cilium occupying a volume of characteristic size 10 μm, in good agreement with the values reported in the literature (Hill et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the model fitting, with a citation.

claim: The inclusion of a linear force profile does not significantly alter the predicted velocity profile.
source: We report that the inclusion of a linear force profile does not significantly alter the predicted velocity profile (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), which shows the robustness of this averaged model.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from model refinements, with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The model can efficiently predict flow profiles for many other aspect ratios between the cilia extension and any other channel diameter and heterogenous ciliary beating frequency.
source: Interestingly, our model can efficiently predict flow profiles for many other aspect ratios between the cilia extension and any other channel diameter and heterogenous ciliary beating frequency (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated as a finding about the model's versatility, with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The model convincingly predicts the flow previously reported by Shields et al. (2010) in the context of artificial magnetic cilia in microchannels.
source: It convincingly predicts the flow previously reported by Shields et al. (2010) in the context of artificial magnetic cilia in microchannels , where this aspect ratio is low.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with previous work, with a citation.

claim: The contribution of dorsal cilia was neglected in the model (although they represent about 20 % of all motile cilia).
source: We also neglected the contribution of dorsal cilia (although they represent about 20 % of all motile cilia), and we now provide further justifications for this choice.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the modeling approach.

claim: The dorsal cilia, also oriented in the caudal direction, tend to cancel the contribution of their neighboring ventral cilia.
source: The dorsal cilia, also oriented in the caudal direction, tend to cancel the contribution of their neighboring ventral cilia.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for neglecting dorsal cilia.

claim: Locally, beating dorsal cilia can abolish the bidirectional flow and create recirculation regions.
source: Locally, beating dorsal cilia can thus abolish the bidirectional flow and create recirculation regions.
evidence: This is stated as an inference about the effect of dorsal cilia.

claim: The bidirectional flow is affected by at most 20% due to the presence of sparse dorsal cilia.
source: The bidirectional flow is thus affected by at most 20% due to the presence of sparse dorsal cilia.
evidence: This is stated as an estimate of the effect of dorsal cilia.

claim: The presence of the Reissner fiber in the central canal was neglected in the model.
source: The presence of the RF in the central canal was also neglected here, although it was proven to play a critical role in body axis straightening (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the modeling approach, with a citation.

claim: As the Reissner fiber does not compartmentalize the fluid in 3D, its presence should not qualitatively modify the nature of the flow and its bidirectionality.
source: As the RF does not compartmentalize the fluid in 3D, its presence should not qualitatively modify the nature of the flow and its bidirectionality.
evidence: This is stated as a justification for neglecting the Reissner fiber.

claim: Velocity profiles measured in scospondin mutants that lack a Reissner fiber confirm that the Reissner fiber does not qualitatively modify the flow.
source: This is confirmed by velocity profiles measured in scospondin mutants that lack a RF (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a confirmation from experimental data, with a citation.

claim: A change of activity of CSF-contacting neurons in the absence of the Reissner fiber may occur.
source: As CSF-contacting neurons are known to be mechanosensitive (Jalalvand et al., 2016; Sternberg et al., 2018), a change of activity of these neurons in the absence of the RF may also occur.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation, with citations.

claim: The working model to account for the curved body axis of ciliary mutants is that the lack of motile cilia abolishes CSF flow, which leads to a reduction in central canal diameter that alters Reissner fiber polymerization.
source: Our working model to account for the curved body axis of ciliary mutants is that the lack of motile cilia abolishes CSF flow, which leads to a reduction in CC diameter that alters RF polymerization (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018), and would alter the expression of URP peptides in CSF-contacting neurons (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a working model, with citations.

claim: The lack of motile cilia would alter the expression of URP peptides in CSF-contacting neurons.
source: Our working model to account for the curved body axis of ciliary mutants is that the lack of motile cilia abolishes CSF flow, which leads to a reduction in CC diameter that alters RF polymerization (Cantaut-Belarif et al., 2018), and would alter the expression of URP peptides in CSF-contacting neurons (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as part of a working model, with a citation.

claim: The transparency of zebrafish embryos allows characterization of CSF bidirectional flow and cilia dynamics in the central canal.
source: Here, we take advantage of the transparency of zebrafish embryos to characterize CSF bidirectional flow and cilia dynamics in the CC.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for using zebrafish.

claim: The structure of the central canal is very challenging to access with optical imaging in most species, but is well conserved among vertebrates.
source: As the structure of the CC is very challenging to access with optical imaging in most species, but is well conserved among vertebrates (Orts-Del'Immagine and Wyart, 2017), we expect that our findings in zebrafish will guide future investigations in mammals.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for the study's relevance, with a citation.

claim: The findings in zebrafish are expected to guide future investigations in mammals.
source: As the structure of the CC is very challenging to access with optical imaging in most species, but is well conserved among vertebrates (Orts-Del'Immagine and Wyart, 2017), we expect that our findings in zebrafish will guide future investigations in mammals.
evidence: This is stated as an expectation about the study's impact.

claim: The CSF flow is expected to differ at later stages, as both the structure and the motility of cilia change over time in the central canal.
source: We expect the CSF flow to differ at later stages, as both the structure and the motility of cilia change over time in the CC.
evidence: This is stated as an expectation about future findings.

claim: CSF transport may impact development, inflammatory response, and modulation of locomotor and postural functions carried by motor circuits.
source: Altogether, by combining models and quantitative data to demonstrate the origin and the role of the bidirectional flow, our study is a major step towards the understanding of CSF transport and its contribution to long-range communication between cells throughout the body that may well impact development, inflammatory response, and modulation of locomotor and postural functions carried by motor circuits.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation about the broader implications of the study.
